    About me

    Dell Premier · B2B e-commerce

    Dell Premier Homepage Redesign

    Premier Homepage is the central hub where business customers shop for and manage end-to-end solutions through a simple, personalized online platform. I co-led the research and strategy, and the redesign lifted order value and revenue per visit.

    Role
    Research Co-Lead & Product Design
    Timeline
    Sept 2023 – Jul 2024 · launched Oct 2024
    Awards
    President’s Award · Game Changer Award
    Prototype
    Prototype ↗

    +9.9%

    average order value

    +7.1%

    revenue per visit

    4 mo

    Phase 2 redesign, delivered with a new team

    00 — Problem

    Customers couldn’t navigate Premier

    Customers were having difficulty navigating Premier, prompting them to contact sales representatives or leave Premier entirely.

    01 — Discovery

    Listening to stakeholders and customers

    Stakeholder research: 6 workshops with the Premier HP stakeholders, 2 with the global merchandising team, and 1 ideation and 1 problem statement workshop with the core team.

    Customer research: 10 Premier customers across medium business, commercial, channel and sales representatives. The goal was to uncover gaps in their journey, validate expectations and test hypotheses.

    • 10/10 want to talk to their sales representatives to purchase and update products, because it’s easier than doing it themselves
    • 10/10 want to place bulk orders quickly, but struggle with the current interface
    • 10/10 don’t find the current homepage content useful, since they rarely buy outside their preconfigured products
    • 9/10 want to customize Premier to suit their needs

    Stakeholders flagged clarity, information access and personalization, automation of common actions, collaborative shopping, and notifications such as expiring quotes.

    02 — Framing

    How might we…

    • get customers the information they need, so they don’t have to rely on sales representatives?
    • help customers quickly access the Premier features they use most and that matter to them?
    • give each user type (shopper, buyer, admin) a valuable, delightful, tailored experience?
    • personalize the homepage based on the customer’s intent?

    03 — Design iterations

    We iterated on the designs based on the research

    Each iteration tested one of the insights from discovery.

    04 — Feedback

    What customers said about the new design

    90% of customers liked the new design because it gives them tailored data for their business.

    They also pointed to a few opportunity areas:

    • Wouldn’t scroll past the dashboard to explore other areas (4/11)
    • Didn’t like the advertising banner (3/11)
    • Didn’t order new products, so popular products weren’t needed (2/11)

    Based on this feedback, Phase 2 focused on strengthening the Dell Premier experience.

    05 — Final design

    Quick access first, then purchase history

    I prioritized quick access to the most frequently used features and key customer information.

    Next, I used purchase history to surface frequently bought items for faster reordering.

    Finally, I placed support and spotlight sections at the bottom of the page to finish the journey.

    06 — Before and after

    Before and after

    Results

    What changed

    • +9.9% increase in average order value (AOV)
    • +7.1% increase in revenue per visit (RPV)
    • Customers find key information and features without relying on sales representatives
    • Personalized experiences for shoppers, buyers and admins

    Dell Premier · Landing page

    Dell Premier Landing Page Redesign

    The Premier Landing Page is Dell’s public introduction to the Premier platform. I led the redesign so business customers could quickly understand what Premier offers and why it matters to them.

    Role
    Project Lead & Product Design
    Timeline
    July 2024 – March 2025 · launched April 2025

    +2.8×

    growth in new account submissions

    +19%

    increase in sign-ins

    +70%

    traffic to the page

    00 — Problem

    A landing page without a clear value story

    Dell Premier lacked a clear brand identity and a consistent value proposition, which made it hard to attract new customers and build loyalty.

    01 — Discovery

    Competitors and customers

    I ran a competitive analysis of 20+ companies, then reviewed internal and external qualitative research.

    • Unique value: what is the unique value of Dell Premier compared with other competitors?
    • Dell branding: users expect Premier to be the final layer of what Dell offers customers
    • Customer-centric benefits: users want to know what they will get, not just what we offer

    02 — Framing

    What the page needed to do

    Users wanted to quickly scan the content, and they needed shorter videos that get to the point.

    • Design workshops: user flow, content strategy and framework, wireframes, hi-fi design and prototypes
    • Unmoderated user testing: 3 rounds with SMB, large and enterprise customers

    03 — Final design

    A landing page that explains Premier quickly

    The new Premier Landing Page makes it easier for customers to quickly understand Premier’s value. Clear, scannable benefits, an interactive Premier Tour, and data-driven impact stories help users see how Dell Premier can support their business.

    With added FAQs to address common questions, we reduced uncertainty and helped customers onboard more confidently.

    04 — Before and after

    Before and after

    Results

    What changed

    • +2.8× growth in new account submissions
    • +19% increase in sign-ins
    • +70% increase in traffic to the page
    • Drove organic growth of B2B leads, serving as an acquisition channel for new business accounts

    ShelterTech · Accessibility

    Accessibility Audit Driving 100% Issue Resolution on ShelterTech.org

    ShelterTech.org is a San Francisco nonprofit that bridges the digital divide through technology. I led accessibility audits for ShelterTech.org and SFServiceGuide.org, then turned the findings into fixes the team could carry forward on its own.

    Role
    Inclusive Design Lead (Accessibility)
    Timeline
    Jan 2023 – Apr 2023
    Standard
    WCAG 2.1 A and AA

    37% → 0%

    ShelterTech.org failure rate

    24%

    SFServiceGuide.org failure rate, all critical and high issues fixed

    60+

    WCAG 2.1 criteria tested

    01 — Audit

    Finding the gaps

    I audited both platforms against WCAG 2.1 A and AA. The audits uncovered failure rates of 37% on ShelterTech.org and 24% on SFServiceGuide.org. I turned the findings into prioritized, actionable fixes.

    02 — Enablement

    Building capability, not just fixing issues

    I created a “How to Test for Accessibility” training deck and a step-by-step checklist, so developers could test and remediate issues on their own. The goal was to strengthen compliance over the long term and build a culture of inclusive design across the team.

    Results

    What changed

    • ShelterTech.org: reduced the accessibility failure rate from 37% to 0%, with full WCAG 2.1 AA compliance
    • SFServiceGuide.org: identified a 24% failure rate, with all critical and high-severity issues remediated
    • Across both platforms: 0 remaining critical accessibility blockers
    • Tested against 60+ WCAG 2.1 criteria at the A and AA levels
